FP1.reason: The password is checked in browser JavaScript, not on a server.

FP2.reason: There is no functional shared download service or server-side password enforcement; the file exists only in browser memory.

FP3.reason: The password is stored in plaintext in an in-memory browser map.

FP1.reason: The password is checked entirely in the browser using client-side JavaScript and is stored in plain text in memory.

FP2.reason: The file can be downloaded without a password if an attacker inspects the JavaScript and reconstructs the blob URL or accesses the in-memory fileStorage map.

FP3.reason: The password is stored in plain text in the fileStorage Map without any hashing.

FP1.reason: There is no server; the password is stored in a browser-side Map and compared in client-side JavaScript.

FP2.reason: There is no server or access control, and files live only in the uploader's browser memory, so nothing enforces a password on any direct URL.

FP3.reason: The password is stored in plain text in the in-memory object and compared directly, with no hashing.
